correctness.rationale: Exact Zak diagonalization at integer redundancy yields the scalar squared-multiplier sum; the two geometric tails give a positive fractional-cosine expression strictly increasing in frequency cosine. The positive upper branch is strictly convex with equal endpoints, while the lower branch has one positive-root derivative and coincident endpoints; strict Cauchy-Schwarz for m>=2 proves A>0. Endpoints are essential spectral edges. The packaged program executed 4800 direct comparisons; these are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Quantifies sharp stability for a natural previously qualitatively classified two-rate nonsymmetric window. For every integer oversampling and all two positive decay parameters it replaces two-dimensional spectral optimization by finite sums and a single quadratic root, additionally locating the unique worst Zak fiber. This is a complete natural family result, not a trivial rephrasing of frame membership or of symmetric sharp lattice estimates.
